'''Liliana Quintanar Vera''' (born 1975) is a Mexican chemist. She works on proteins and neurodegenerative diseases.

== Early life and education ==
Quintanar Vera was born in [[Mexico City]] in 1975.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://www.amc.edu.mx/amc/|title=Inicio|website=www.amc.edu.mx|access-date=2018-12-24}}</ref> She took part in the [[Mexican Academy of Sciences]] Chemistry Olympics, representing the country in the [[International Chemistry Olympiad]] in 1993.<ref name=":0" /> She studied chemistry at [[National Autonomous University of Mexico]] in 1998.<ref name=":0" /> She was awarded the Gabino Barreda medal. She took part in an exchange program with the [[University of California, Santa Barbara]].<ref name=":0" /> She worked on [[Neurochemistry]] with Stanley Parsons. Quintanar Vera joined [[Stanford University]] for her PhD, working on [[metalloprotein]]s under the supervision of [[Edward I. Solomon]]. She focussed on the structure, function and activation mechanism of [[multicopper oxidase]].

== Career ==
Quintanar Vera returned to Mexico and join the [[National Autonomous University of Mexico]] Department of Neurochemistry of the Institute of Physiology. She worked on [[manganese]] neurotoxicity.<ref name=":0" /> She joined [[CINVESTAV]] in 2005, where she studies the proteins associated with [[Neurodegeneration|neurodegenerative]] diseases.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.sqm.org.mx/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=213:webinar-sqm-liliana-quinanar&catid=2&Itemid=200|title=Sociedad Química de México. A.C. - Webinar - SQM Liliana Quintanar|website=www.sqm.org.mx|access-date=2018-12-24}}</ref> [[Alzheimer's disease]] can cause proteins to aggregate and accumulate metals.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=http://www.cronica.com.mx/notas/2018/1060501.html|title=Desbalance de cobre en el cerebro, clave en el desarrollo de Alzheimer {{!}} La Crónica de Hoy|website=www.cronica.com.mx|access-date=2018-12-24|archive-date=2019-04-01|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190401140057/http://www.cronica.com.mx/notas/2018/1060501.html|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name="elsiglodetorreon.com.mx">{{Cite web|url=https://www.elsiglodetorreon.com.mx/noticia/661999.metales-podrian-relacionarse-con-mal-de-alzheimer.html|title=Metales podrían relacionarse con mal de Alzheimer|date=2011-09-20|website=www.elsiglodetorreon.com.mx|language=es-MX|access-date=2018-12-24}}</ref> She studies the role of metals in the aggregation of proteins and the [[etiology]] of diseases.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|url=https://www.la-prensa.com.mx/ciencia-y-tecnologia/245986-galardonaran-a-quimica-del-cinvestav-ipn|title=Galardonarán a Química del Cinvestav IPN|date=13 November 2017<!-- , 4:49 pm-->|website=La Prensa|access-date=2018-12-24|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190401141327/https://www.la-prensa.com.mx/ciencia-y-tecnologia/245986-galardonaran-a-quimica-del-cinvestav-ipn|archive-date=1 April 2019|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Quintanar Vera was a [[Fulbright scholar]] at [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] working with Jonathan King between 2014 and 2015.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":3">{{Cite web|url=https://www.cies.org/grantee/liliana-quintanar-vera|title=Liliana Quintanar Vera {{!}} Fulbright Scholar Program|website=www.cies.org|access-date=2018-12-24}}</ref> Her project looked at the role of copper ions in human [[Gamma crystallin|Gamma-D crystallin]].<ref name=":3" />  Quintanar Vera was appointed to the Society International Biological Inorganic Chemistry in 2017.<ref name=":0" /> In 2017 she coordinated the Thematic Network of Structure, Function and Evolution of Proteins (REFEP).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.elsoldecuautla.com.mx/local/promueven-la-vinculacion-cientifica-2119758.html|title=Promueven la vinculación científica|last=Arellano|first=Jessica|website=El Sol de Cuautla|language=es|access-date=2018-12-24}}</ref>
